action: Maersk customers and partners: watch for company updates on what data was involved, be alert to invoices or shipping messages that look unusual, and verify any payment-detail change by phone.
exec: An inherited legacy system gave attackers a way in at a major logistics firm; Maersk says no sensitive data has been disclosed.
plain: Shipping company Maersk confirmed that an intruder took data from an older system it gained through an acquisition. A criminal group called WhiteArmor demands $5 million and threatens to publish about 100GB of data.
summary: Maersk said an intruder reached a legacy system inherited through an acquisition and extracted data. The WhiteArmor group claimed the attack and threatened to publish about 100GB from a logistics platform unless paid $5 million. Maersk says no sensitive data has been disclosed.
title: Maersk confirms data theft; WhiteArmor demands $5 million

validation.note: Company confirmation reported by BleepingComputer and a second roundup.
